meta.description: LeieXEie — compare renting and buying with Norwegian tax and finance rules. Educational tool, not financial advice.

header.tagline: Your smart guide to choosing whether to rent or own a home in Norway.
header.step1: Pick a city or enter your own numbers

mode.quickDesc: Rent, price, loan and time — the core comparison
mode.advancedDesc: Co-op debt, taxes, savings and ownership costs

inputs.years: Years You Plan to Live There
inputs.isCouple: We are a couple taxed jointly for wealth tax
inputs.bsuActive: I save in BSU (under 34 and first-time buyer)
inputs.rentalIncome: Rental Income From Letting Part of the Home

tooltips.monthlyRent: Your current monthly rent. Used as the baseline cost for the renting scenario.
tooltips.rentIncrease: How much your landlord raises the rent each year. Norwegian average is around 3–5%.
tooltips.purchasePrice: The asking price of the home you want to buy.
tooltips.downPayment: Auto-set to 15% of the purchase price. Norwegian lending rules (utlånsforskriften) require at least a 10% down payment.
tooltips.mortgageRate: The annual interest rate on your mortgage. Check with your bank for a current offer.
tooltips.loanTermYears: How many years until your mortgage is fully paid off. 25–30 years is most common in Norway.
tooltips.monthlyHoaFee: Monthly joint costs in a shared housing cooperative — includes maintenance, insurance, and management fees.
tooltips.stampDuty: Auto-set to 2.5% of the purchase price. In advanced mode, a housing cooperative sets this to 0. For a new build the fee is often only on the plot value — adjust the amount yourself.
tooltips.otherClosingCosts: Other one-time costs at purchase: tinglysning (deed + mortgage registration), bank setup fees, etc. Typically 5,000–15,000 kr.
tooltips.brokerSellingFee: A typical broker fee in Norway is around 100,000 kr or 1–3% of the sale price. Enter it in today's prices – it grows with house prices until you sell.
tooltips.sharedDebt: Shared debt in a borettslag that transfers with the unit. Affects total cost and tax deductions.
tooltips.municipalFees: Annual municipal fees covering water, sewage, and waste collection. Typically 10,000–20,000 kr/year.
tooltips.renovationPct: Annual maintenance budget as a percentage of the home's value. A common rule of thumb is 0.5–1% per year.
tooltips.homeInsurance: Annual insurance for the building structure. Usually 5,000–15,000 kr/year depending on size.
tooltips.propertyTax: Property tax charged by some Norwegian municipalities. Many municipalities charge 0%. Check your local rate.
tooltips.hoaFeeIncrease: How much the HOA / shared costs rise each year. Boards typically adjust annually in line with costs.
tooltips.years: How long you plan to stay. The longer you own, the more the upfront buying costs are spread out.
tooltips.appreciationRate: Norwegian average home price growth is approximately 2–4% per year. Enter a negative number to see what happens if prices fall.
tooltips.investmentReturn: Expected annual interest on a regular savings account, before tax. Quick mode assumes the money is kept in a savings account, so 22% tax on the interest is deducted every year (automatically applied). Norwegian savings accounts typically pay 3–5% per year.
tooltips.contentsInsurance: Insurance for your belongings (innbo). Needed both when renting and owning. Typically 1,500–3,000 kr/year.
tooltips.electricity: Annual electricity and heating costs. Varies widely — roughly 15,000–30,000 kr/year for an apartment.
tooltips.internet: Annual broadband cost. Typically around 4,000–6,000 kr/year in Norway.
tooltips.parking: Monthly parking cost if applicable. Applies both when renting and owning. Leave at 0 if included.
tooltips.sharedDebtRate: The interest rate on the housing cooperative's shared debt (fellesgjeld). This interest is included in monthly HOA fees and is also tax-deductible. Typically close to the current mortgage rate.
tooltips.interestOnlyYears: Number of years paying interest only (avdragsfrihet), with no principal repayment. After this period the full loan amortises over the remaining term. Many Norwegian banks offer up to 5 years.
tooltips.inflation: General price growth used to convert future amounts to today's money. Norwegian long-run target is 2%.
tooltips.savingsAccountBalance: Savings you have in addition to the down payment, kept as a liquid buffer. Both buyer and renter keep it. Interest is taxed annually at 22% (automatically applied).
tooltips.savingsAccountRate: Interest rate on your savings account. Check with your bank. 22% tax on interest is automatically applied.
tooltips.askBalance: Funds you have in an Aksjesparekonto (ASK) in addition to the down payment. Both buyer and renter keep it. Grows tax-free until withdrawal — 37.84% capital gains tax is modelled automatically.
tooltips.askRate: Expected annual return on shares/funds in an Aksjesparekonto (ASK). Historical average ~7% per year. Capital gains tax of 37.84% (Norwegian shareholder model) is applied only on withdrawal — modelled automatically.
tooltips.askShieldingRate: The shielding deduction (skjermingsfradrag) reduces taxable ASK gains. Skatteetaten sets the rate annually (typically 3–5%). Only gains above accumulated shielding are taxed at 37.84%.
tooltips.bsuActive: BSU (Boligsparing for ungdom): save up to 27,500 kr/year and get a 10% tax deduction (max 2,750 kr/year). Available until age 34 if you haven't used BSU for a purchase. The deduction reduces the cost of renting, and the contribution earns your savings-account rate instead of the ASK return.
tooltips.bsuYearlyContribution: Amount you save in BSU this year. Max 27,500 kr per person (2026), so 55,000 kr for a couple. You get 10% back as a tax deduction. The contribution itself stays in BSU at your savings-account rate.
tooltips.isBorettslag: Tick if the home is in a borettslag. No stamp duty (dokumentavgift) is paid, and you can enter the shared debt (fellesgjeld). Leave unticked for selveier/sameie, where 2.5% stamp duty applies.
tooltips.sharedDebtTermYears: Remaining repayment term on the cooperative's shared debt. Your share is paid down through the monthly HOA fee, so your remaining shared debt falls over time. Set 0 if the loan is interest-only.
tooltips.mortgageRateChangeYear: The year a new mortgage rate takes effect, e.g. when a fixed-rate period ends or you expect rates to fall. The payment is recalculated on the remaining loan. Set 0 for no change.
tooltips.mortgageRateAfterChange: The mortgage rate that applies from the chosen year until the end of the period.
tooltips.isCouple: Married, registered partners or cohabitants taxed jointly get double the wealth-tax allowance (3,800,000 kr instead of 1,900,000 kr). Applies to both buyer and renter.
tooltips.householdIncome: Combined income before tax for everyone on the mortgage. Used to check the rule that total debt cannot exceed 5 times income. Leave at 0 to skip the check.
tooltips.otherDebt: Debt you already have, such as student loans, car loans and credit cards. Banks include it in the debt-to-income ratio, and the stress test prices it as interest-only at the stress rate.
tooltips.rentalIncome: Monthly rent if you let out part of the home, such as a bedsit (hybel) or basement flat. It is tax-free when you let out less than half of the home, measured by rental value. It rises each year in line with rent.

footer.disclaimer: For educational purposes only. Not financial advice.

warnings.downPaymentTooLow: Below the {{pct}}% minimum down payment banks require.
warnings.downPaymentTooHigh: The down payment is higher than the purchase price.
warnings.downPaymentTooLowShared: Below the {{pct}}% minimum down payment — for a borettslag the shared debt counts towards the price.
warnings.debtToIncome: Total debt would be {{value}} times income. Banks normally cannot lend more than {{max}} times gross annual income.

sensitivity.caption: Buy versus rent advantage by {{row}} and {{col}}

cellTitle.buy: Buying wins by {{amount}} when {{row}} is {{rowValue}} and {{col}} is {{colValue}}
cellTitle.rent: Renting wins by {{amount}} when {{row}} is {{rowValue}} and {{col}} is {{colValue}}

sensitivity.note: Everything else is kept as you entered it. A rate change later in the period moves by the same amount. In advanced mode the return applies to the ASK account.

results.title: Your Rent vs Buy Analysis
results.stressTestHint: Banks must check that you can afford a rate 3 percentage points higher than today, and at least 7% (utlånsforskriften). Includes higher interest on shared debt, and other debt priced at the stress rate.
results.splitTitle: Renting and buying side by side
results.unitsNote: Equity and portfolio are in today's NOK. Mortgage payment, total paid and home value are nominal amounts.

recommendation.buyDesc: After {{years}} years, owning puts you {{amount}} ahead. Your net proceeds after selling the home come to {{equity}}, versus the {{portfolio}} you'd have built by renting and investing the difference.
recommendation.rentDesc: After {{years}} years, renting and investing puts you {{amount}} ahead. Your investment portfolio of {{portfolio}} grows larger than the {{equity}} you'd walk away with after selling the home.
recommendation.breakevenAt: The two paths cross at year {{year}} — before that, the other option was ahead.
recommendation.noBreakevenBuy: Buying stays ahead for the entire {{years}}-year period.
recommendation.noBreakevenRent: Renting stays ahead for the entire {{years}}-year period.
recommendation.realTermsNote: All figures are in today's money — adjusted for inflation.
recommendation.disclaimer: This is an estimate based on your inputs and assumptions about future market conditions. Always consult a qualified financial advisor before making major financial decisions.
recommendation.thresholdRent: Owning wins when rent is above {{amount}} per month. You entered {{current}}.
recommendation.thresholdAppreciation: Owning wins when house prices grow faster than {{rate}} a year. You entered {{current}}.

affordability.noteOk: Total debt is within the limit of {{max}} times gross annual income (utlånsforskriften). The bank will also check that you can afford the stress-test rate after normal living costs.
affordability.noteOver: Total debt is {{over}} above the limit of {{max}} times gross annual income (utlånsforskriften). Banks only have a small quota for exceptions, so you will likely need more equity, less other debt or a cheaper home.

breakdown.title: Calculation Details
breakdown.formulaL: the amount you borrow from the bank ({{amount}})
breakdown.formulaR: monthly interest rate — the annual rate divided by 12 ({{rate}})
breakdown.formulaNAfterIo: number of monthly payments after the interest-only period ({{count}})
breakdown.formulaExplainer: The formula gives a fixed monthly amount (annuity). Early on most of it is interest; later more of it pays down the loan.
breakdown.initialInvestmentNote: Invested in the market instead of buying (down payment + closing costs)
breakdown.initialInvestmentAskNote: invested in ASK instead of buying
breakdown.securityDepositNote: held in a deposit account earning savings interest, returned at move-out
breakdown.quickTaxNote: Assumes a regular savings account: {{pct}}% tax on interest every year, applied automatically
breakdown.monthlyDiffNote: Each month, whichever side has lower costs invests the difference
breakdown.tableNote: Net worth figures are in real terms (inflation-adjusted). Bold value is leading that year.
breakdown.wealthTaxHome: Primary residence: {{pct}}% of market value up to {{threshold}}
breakdown.wealthTaxHomeTiered: Primary residence above {{threshold}}: {{pct}}% of the excess
breakdown.taxFreeHomeSale: Capital gain on home sale is tax-free (primary residence, owned & lived in 12 of last 24 months)
breakdown.shieldingNote: Shielding deduction ({{rate}}%/yr) has been applied to ASK gains
breakdown.bsuBenefit: BSU deduction: {{amount}} per year. The contribution earns the savings-account rate, not the ASK return
breakdown.askCapitalGainsTax: ASK capital gains tax after shielding ({{pct}}%)
breakdown.rateChangeNote: From year {{year}} the rate is {{rate}}%: payment is recalculated to {{payment}} / month on the remaining loan

pdf.investReturnLine: Savings account interest: {{return}}%/yr ({{pct}}% tax yearly, auto)
pdf.monthlyDiffShort: Monthly difference → invested by the cheaper side
pdf.realTermsNote: All net worth figures are in real (inflation-adjusted) terms
pdf.yearByYearSubtitle: All net worth figures in real terms – adjusted for {{inflation}}% inflation per year
pdf.notesBuyerEquity: · Buyer net worth = Home value − Mortgage − Shared debt − Selling costs + Savings/ASK, inflation-adjusted
pdf.notesRenterEquity: · Renter's net worth = Investment portfolio after estimated tax, inflation-adjusted
pdf.notesDisclaimer: · This model is indicative. Always consult a financial advisor for major decisions.
